jargon_glossary.meaning: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.

jargon_glossary.meaning: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.

jargon_glossary.term: Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)
jargon_glossary.meaning: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.

jargon_glossary.term: TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)
jargon_glossary.meaning: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.

# What's New in VLLM v0.26.0: The Adoption Decision Guide

> **Positioning**: *Translating VLLM v0.26.0 implementation changes into adoption decisions for people who don't follow inference engineering full-time — what changed, and what it means for the models you serve, the GPUs you own, and your inference bill.*

**Release Snapshot**: `42` upstream changes analyzed | `8` capability themes | `4` upgrade/deprecation notices | `11` quantified performance proofs

---

## 1. What's the Big Deal?

Instead of reading hundreds of isolated PR descriptions, here are the most consequential architectural shifts in this release and why they matter operationally:

1. **Frontier MoE & Sparse-MLA Speedups (DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3)** ([#48660](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48660), [#47463](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47463), [#48137](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48137), [#47327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47327))
   - **What changed**: DeepSeek-V4: specialized routing kernel (2.94% E2E TPOT, #48660), `fused_topk_bias` 1.5–2x (#47463), redundant repeat/copy removal (1.8% TPOT, #48137).; MLA: dense MHA path for short sparse-MLA sequences (#47327); MiniMax-M3 long-context decode indexer on sm100 (#48582).; Decode Context Parallel (DCP): hybrid attention support (#40996), DCP + Eagle for Tokenspeed MLA backends (#48180).; FlashAttention 3 pinned to the torch stable-ABI commit (#47995); ABI-stable FlashMLA build (#48174).; MLA: `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` support (#47309).
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **Frontier Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning and agentic models (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3/K3.1, MiniMax-M3.1)** on **NVIDIA Blackwell (GB200/GB300/B200), Hopper (H100/H200), and multi-node Expert Parallel (EP) clusters** — **Delivers 1.24x–1.95x higher throughput and faster long-prompt TTFT, directly slashing cost-per-million tokens**.
2. **Next-Gen Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3, DSpark, DFlash, MTP & Suffix)** ([#46090](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46090), [#40714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40714), [#48289](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48289), [#47321](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47321))
   - **What changed**: CPU: DFlash speculative decoding for GDN models on CPU (#46090), s390x NUMA topology (#40714), native macOS arm64 CPU wheel builds (#48289); POWER VSX math function...; Reasoning: optimize TPOT for thinking budget when used with speculative decoding (#46662).; Speculative decoding: runtime draft weight update (#46725), hybrid (SWA + full attention) DFlash drafters (#47914), SWA support for qwen-eagle3 (#47568), Gemma4-12B DSpark...; XPU: batch-invariant kernels (#41934), HND KV layout support (#47975), DSpark spec decode for DSv4 (#47677), nightly/release image publishing (#47880, #48126).; Fixes: host memory leak from undrained `new_block_ids` (#44490), DSv3.2 + MTP + sequence-parallel accuracy (#48036).
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **Interactive coding assistants, agent loops, and low-batch-size real-time inference** on **NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, AMD MI300X/MI355X, and CPU/XPU draft runners** — **Accelerates single-stream decode speed by 1.35x–2.2x using idle GPU memory bandwidth**.
3. **Low-Precision Quantization Kernels (NVFP4, MXFP4, MXFP8, FP8 & Humming)** ([#48688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48688), [#47718](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47718), [#48519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48519), [#48788](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48788))
   - **What changed**: ROCm: fp32 `head_dtype` `torch.mm` fast path (#48688), DSv4 two-stage compressor kernel (#47718), sparse decode/prefill optimizations (#48519, #48788, #46275), DSv3.2 sparse...; NVFP4/MXFP4: `nvfp4_per_token` online MoE quantization (#48538), CuTe-DSL FlashInfer MXFP4 quantization (#48417); bounded peak memory when repacking FP4 MoE weights for Marlin...; ROCm: HybridW4A16 linear kernel (#40977).; Humming w[2-7]a[4,8] weight-only inference with compressed-tensors (#46390); int4 quantization for the emulation MoE backend (#48451); INT2 XPU weight-only quant linear (#47521).
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **100B–1T+ parameter models (Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.5/3.8) quantized to 4-bit/8-bit** on **NVIDIA Blackwell (SM100 NVFP4), Hopper (SM90 FP8), and AMD MI350/MI355X** — **Halves GPU count required to fit 400B–1T weights in VRAM and up to doubles Tensor Core compute throughput**.
4. **Disaggregated Serving (P/D, DCP/PCP), Fault Tolerance & Fast Checkpoint/Restore** ([#48012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48012), [#48011](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48011), [#44455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44455), [#46570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46570))
   - **What changed**: Attention: select a different attention backend per KV-cache group (#48012); sliding-window as an explicit backend capability (#48011); KV-cache layout refactor packing K/V...; Build/autotune: arm64 Blackwell SM10x/SM110 image builds (#48041); skip CuTeDSL fp4_gemm autotuning by default (#48268).; PD disaggregation: NIXL pipeline-parallel prefill in push mode (#45880).
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **Planet-scale distributed inference clusters, serverless GPU autoscalers, and OpenAI Responses API clients** on **Multi-node RDMA / InfiniBand / AWS EFA clusters and Kubernetes inference gateways** — **Eliminates full-cluster restarts when a single GPU rank dies and cuts autoscaling cold-start time via CRIU restore**.
5. **Day-0 Model Architectures, Multimodal Vision/Audio & Transformers Backend** ([#46998](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46998), [#47006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47006), [#48350](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48350), [#47546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47546))
   - **What changed**: Qwen: fuse more RMSNorm + all-reduce in Qwen3.5 (#46998), replace MoE all-reduce with reduce-scatter (#47006), Qwen3.5 H20 optimization (#48350), expand Triton warmup coverage...; New models: Inkling family (#48799, #48822, #48858, #48869, #48884, #48990), BertForMaskedLM (#48463), RobertaForTokenClassification / XLMRobertaForTokenClassification...; LoRA: FlashInfer MoE LoRA for BF16 models (#48632), LoRA for tower/connector in LlavaNextVideo (#48594), fp32 `lm_head` on the LoRA path (#48525), optimized `TrtLlmLoRAExperts`...; Transformers backend migrations: Olmo/Olmo2 (#48100), MistralLarge3 to AutoWeightsLoader (#48153), HunyuanVL native transformers processor for transformers 5.13 (#47872).; Encoder-cache connectors: EC transfer params (#42433) and CPU-offloading EC connector (#47423).
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **Newly released foundation models, Vision-Language (VLM), Speech/ASR (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`), and Multi-LoRA adapters** on **Standard single-node and multi-node GPU inference pools** — **Consolidates text, vision, speech, and embedding models onto a single unified vLLM serving fleet**.
6. **Multi-Vendor Accelerator Scaling (AMD ROCm 10 / MI355X, TPU & XPU)** ([#47973](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47973), [#48335](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48335), [#42562](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42562), [#45182](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45182))
   - **What changed**: MoE router GEMMs: BF16x3 router GEMM (#47973), FP32 router GEMV (#48335), generic CuteDSL LL BF16 router GEMM (#42562); TRTLLM BF16 MoE modular kernel (#45182); write...; Transformers 5.13.0 (#47867), FlashInfer 0.6.14 (#47669), NIXL 1.3.1 (#47559), tpu-inference v0.24.0 (#47835), nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 (#47442), vllm_xpu_kernels v0.1.11.1...
   - **Why it matters**: Directly benefits **Cross-vendor LLM fleets running DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and MiniMax outside CUDA-only clouds** on **AMD Instinct MI300X/MI350/MI355X (ROCm 10.0), Intel XPU, and Google Cloud TPU** — **Enables hardware price-performance arbitrage across AMD and NVIDIA GPU clouds without changing serving code**.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?

Plain-English translations for the systems and inference terms that show up in this release:

- **Extensible KV Cache**: Sizes the GPU Key-Value (KV) cache dynamically from actual free VRAM measured *after* model loading and CUDA graph warmup, rather than guessing via a static `gpu_memory_utilization` fraction.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Unlocks 20–55% more KV token capacity per GPU (higher concurrency & throughput) without risking startup OOM crashes.
- **Model Runner V2 (MRV2)**: vLLM's redesigned GPU execution loop featuring persistent batching, zero-overhead input preparation, unified CUDA graph capture, and native speculative decoding.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Replaces legacy Model Runner V1 as the sole GPU runner; lowers CPU-to-GPU launch overhead and unlocks higher token interactivity.
- **Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3 / DSpark / DFlash / MTP / Suffix)**: Uses a fast draft mechanism (a lightweight head like EAGLE3/DSpark, Multi-Token Prediction layers, or n-gram suffix matching) to propose multiple tokens at once, which the main model verifies in a single forward pass.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Boosts per-user token generation speed (interactivity/TPOT) by 1.4x–2.5x without changing output quality.
- **MLA & Sparse-MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention)**: An attention architecture (used by DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K3, GLM-5) that compresses Key-Value states into a compact latent vector, optionally combined with sparse top-k token indexing.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Slashes KV cache memory footprint on long contexts (32K–128K+), enabling far larger batch sizes per GPU.
- **NVFP4 / MXFP4 / FP8 Quantization**: 4-bit and 8-bit floating-point weight and activation formats accelerated natively by NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350/MI355X Tensor/Matrix cores.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Nearly halves GPU memory vs. FP8 (and 4x vs. BF16) while up to doubling GEMM/MoE throughput on Blackwell and MI355X racks.
- **P/D Disaggregation (Prefill/Decode Split & NIXL)**: Separating compute-bound prompt processing (Prefill) onto one pool of GPUs and memory-bandwidth-bound token generation (Decode) onto another, transferring KV cache over RDMA/NVLink via NIXL.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Stops long incoming prompts from stalling active streaming users, letting you tune GPU ratios independently for TTFT and TPOT SLAs.
- **DCP & PCP (Decode / Prefill Context Parallelism)**: Sharding the KV cache and attention computation of a single long-context sequence across multiple GPUs during prefill (PCP) or decode (DCP).  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Prevents single-GPU KV cache bottlenecks and reduces Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) on 32K–1M token agentic prompts.
- **MoE / MegaMoE & Expert Parallelism (EP / DeepGEMM)**: Specialized kernels and all-to-all communication schedules that route tokens across Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers distributed across many GPUs.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Essential for serving frontier MoE models (DeepSeek-V4, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3) at high tokens/sec per GPU.
- **Piecewise & Breakable CUDA Graphs**: Capturing sequences of GPU kernel launches into replayable graphs (even across dynamic control flow) so the CPU doesn't launch hundreds of tiny kernels per token.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Eliminates CPU bottlenecks during decode, cutting inter-token latency (ITL) by 5–25% without long `torch.compile` warmups.
- **TTFT (Time to First Token) & TPOT / ITL (Time Per Output Token)**: The two core LLM latency SLAs: TTFT measures how fast the first response token appears after a prompt; TPOT/ITL measures how fast subsequent tokens stream.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Directly determines whether an AI coding agent or voice assistant feels snappy or sluggish to end users.
- **Tiered KV Offloading & Prefix Caching**: Evicting and reusing computed KV cache blocks across GPU HBM, host CPU DRAM, local NVMe, or shared object storage instead of recomputing shared system prompts.  
  *Bottom line for operators*: Dramatically lowers prefill compute cost and TTFT for multi-turn chat and agent workloads that share long context prefixes.
